Reading / source anchor: Neuronal Dynamics Ch. 1–2 + physiology membrane concepts
Learning outcome: Own membrane RC analogy, ionic currents, resting potential and spike-generation models.
Closed-book regeneration: Derive leaky integrate-and-fire equation and time constant.
Build / reproduction: Simulate current-to-spike response; compare LIF with richer nonlinear/spiking model.
Frontier/current anchor: Neuronal Dynamics provides online theory plus Python exercises.
Oral defense: What biological features does LIF deliberately discard?
Weekly gate: Pass if simplification is tied to intended decoding/control task.

Learning outcome: Understand conductance-based dynamics, threshold, refractory behavior and adaptation.
Closed-book regeneration: Reconstruct current-balance equation and gating-variable concept.
Build / reproduction: Simulate HH-like model under current steps; map excitability regimes.
Frontier/current anchor: Mechanistic models are useful for stimulation and interpretation even when decoders are learned.
Oral defense: Which parameters are physiologically identifiable from extracellular signals?
Weekly gate: Pass if model/measurement observability is discussed.

Learning outcome: Represent spike timing/rates, tuning curves and variability.
Closed-book regeneration: Derive firing-rate estimate and Poisson likelihood/basic information intuition.
Build / reproduction: Generate synthetic population code and decode stimulus from rate vs timing features.
Frontier/current anchor: BCI design depends on what information neural activity carries and how stable it is.
Oral defense: What information did binning destroy?
Weekly gate: Pass if decoder comparison uses same latency/data budget.

Learning outcome: Fit probabilistic encoding models and quantify predictive uncertainty.
Closed-book regeneration: Derive Poisson-GLM log likelihood/gradient intuition.
Build / reproduction: Fit GLM to synthetic spikes; inspect residuals and misspecification.
Frontier/current anchor: Modern neural decoding often combines statistical models and deep learning.
Oral defense: Does predictive accuracy imply mechanistic truth?
Weekly gate: Pass if residual structure is checked.

Learning outcome: Decode continuous/discrete intention while propagating uncertainty.
Closed-book regeneration: Derive linear/Kalman decoder and Bayesian classification formulation.
Build / reproduction: Build cursor/kinematic decoder from synthetic neural population data; add drift.
Frontier/current anchor: BCIs are estimators embedded in feedback loops.
Oral defense: What state is user intending versus what state your labels assume?
Weekly gate: Pass if calibration/uncertainty is reported, not accuracy only.

Learning outcome: Handle electrode/unit drift, learning, fatigue and nonstationary mappings.
Closed-book regeneration: Derive recursive/online parameter update and forgetting-factor tradeoff.
Build / reproduction: Simulate decoder drift; compare static, periodically recalibrated and adaptive models.
Frontier/current anchor: Long-term practical BCIs must work outside one lab session.
Oral defense: When does adaptation chase noise or override user learning?
Weekly gate: Pass if adaptation improves long-horizon utility without catastrophic instability.

Learning outcome: Understand invasive/non-invasive signal bandwidth, noise, referencing and artifacts conceptually.
Closed-book regeneration: Build full signal chain/noise budget from neural source to ADC/decoder.
Build / reproduction: Simulate EMG/ECoG/EEG-like signals with line noise/motion artifact; design filtering without erasing target signal.
Frontier/current anchor: Measurement modality constrains achievable information before ML begins.
Oral defense: Which 'neural' feature could actually be artifact?
Weekly gate: Pass if artifact control/negative control is designed.

Learning outcome: Treat communication rate, latency, error correction and user correction as system variables.
Closed-book regeneration: Derive simple bits/minute or task-time utility metric and latency stability effect.
Build / reproduction: Closed-loop cursor/typing simulator: vary decoder error vs latency vs correction ability.
Frontier/current anchor: Clinical usefulness is not captured by offline classification accuracy.
Oral defense: Would you choose a slower, more accurate decoder?
Weekly gate: Pass if metric maps to user task, not abstract model score.

Learning outcome: Understand spinal/cortical motor pathways, proprioception and feedback/feedforward control.
Closed-book regeneration: Draw nested human-device control loops and delays.
Build / reproduction: Model powered-assistance/exoskeleton control with human adaptation.
Frontier/current anchor: Human operator is part of the controller, not an external disturbance.
Oral defense: Who adapts to whom?
Weekly gate: Pass if coupled adaptation is represented.

Learning outcome: Map stimulus transduction, receptive fields and perceptual adaptation to artificial sensory channels.
Closed-book regeneration: Derive dynamic-range/compression mapping for an augmented sensor.
Build / reproduction: Design simulation converting IR/ultrasound sensor values into haptic/auditory code; quantify learnability/information.
Frontier/current anchor: Sensory augmentation requires a human-learning channel, not just more sensors.
Oral defense: What makes a code intuitive versus merely decodable after training?
Weekly gate: Pass if user-learning burden is an explicit metric.

Learning outcome: Understand stimulation as uncertain input to excitable/adaptive tissue; distinguish activation from desired function.
Closed-book regeneration: Build simplified stimulus-response and safety-envelope model.
Build / reproduction: Simulate closed-loop stimulation controller with uncertain thresholds/adaptation; no operational clinical settings.
Frontier/current anchor: Bidirectional interfaces require both decoding and controlled perturbation.
Oral defense: What unintended populations/effects can the stimulation recruit?
Weekly gate: Pass if control uses conservative constraint independent of performance objective.

Reading / source anchor: NIH 2026 home speech-BCI summary + underlying public paper if available
Learning outcome: Backchain a real practical BCI from implant/signal → decoder → synthesis → home use.
Closed-book regeneration: Reconstruct architecture, training, latency and evaluation metrics from sources.
Build / reproduction: Build reduced speech/sequence-decoding analogue on public/synthetic data.
Frontier/current anchor: NIH reported July 2026 home use of a speech BCI by a person with paralysis.
Oral defense: What changed when the system moved from lab to home?
Weekly gate: Replication Gate: distinguish reported evidence from your extrapolation.

Learning outcome: Understand circulation/gas exchange and compensatory control as engineered-system analogues.
Closed-book regeneration: Derive cardiac output, oxygen delivery and ventilation mass-balance relations.
Build / reproduction: Build lumped cardio-respiratory model under exercise/altitude/device assistance.
Frontier/current anchor: Neurotech often interacts with whole-body physiology.
Oral defense: Which compensation hides device failure until late?
Weekly gate: Pass if multiple feedback loops interact.

Learning outcome: Model slow hormonal/autonomic loops and multi-timescale homeostasis.
Closed-book regeneration: Derive negative-feedback hormone toy model.
Build / reproduction: Simulate fast neural + slow endocrine control of one physiological variable.
Frontier/current anchor: Human augmentation cannot assume one control timescale.
Oral defense: How does delay produce overshoot/oscillation in physiology?
Weekly gate: Pass if timescale separation guides controller design.

Learning outcome: Understand clearance, fluid balance and biochemical regulation relevant to artificial-organ interfaces.
Closed-book regeneration: Derive clearance/mass-balance model.
Build / reproduction: Simulate dialysis/insulin-like control abstraction with sensor delay and safety bounds.
Frontier/current anchor: Artificial organs are cyber-physiological systems.
Oral defense: What does replacing average function miss about homeostatic regulation?
Weekly gate: Pass if disturbance recovery and fault state are tested.

Learning outcome: Define user utility, communication independence, fatigue, training burden and durability endpoints.
Closed-book regeneration: Write target-trial/longitudinal evaluation for assistive neurotechnology.
Build / reproduction: Design synthetic longitudinal dataset and analyze dropout/adaptation/confounding.

Oral defense: Whose definition of success is in the objective?
Weekly gate: Pass if endpoint set includes patient/user-reported and functional measures.

Learning outcome: Treat neural/physiological data as high-stakes signals with consent, access, inference and misuse risks.
Closed-book regeneration: Build threat model and authorization/recourse map.
Build / reproduction: Red-team a BCI data pipeline for inference, insider, model-update and device-control abuse.
Frontier/current anchor: Neural interfaces collapse boundaries between measurement and intervention.
Oral defense: What data/inference should never be required to use the device?
Weekly gate: Pass if local fail-safe and user override are explicit.

Learning outcome: Guarantee bounded behavior under decoder/stimulator/sensor failure.
Closed-book regeneration: Derive invariant/safe-set constraint for simplified assistive controller.
Build / reproduction: Inject drift, dropout, adversarial artifact and actuator saturation into closed-loop simulator.

Oral defense: Which failure mode is detectable before harm?
Weekly gate: Pass if independent monitor catches unsafe command path.

Learning outcome: Create taxonomy: signal, decoder, user adaptation, physiology, interface, task, safety.
Closed-book regeneration: Build causal graph and rank by severity/frequency/tractability.
Build / reproduction: Generate 100 simulated failure episodes and classify mechanisms.
Frontier/current anchor: The research target should be persistent failure, not leaderboard fashion.
Oral defense: Which failures are fundamentally information-limited?
Weekly gate: Pass if taxonomy predicts intervention class.

Learning outcome: Practice reproducible decoding/encoding research.
Closed-book regeneration: Reconstruct preprocessing, train/test split, temporal leakage and metric.
Build / reproduction: Reproduce central decoding result and rerun with session/subject-held-out split.

Oral defense: Does performance survive new-day/new-subject evaluation?
Weekly gate: Extension Gate: reproduction + leakage/OOD audit.

Learning outcome: Design extension improving robust user utility rather than offline score.

Build / reproduction: Implement adaptation, uncertainty, active calibration or feedback change; pre-register test.

Oral defense: What user population/context could be harmed by your adaptation?

Learning outcome: Backchain prototype to power, telemetry, packaging, calibration, maintenance and update lifecycle.

Build / reproduction: Design field-deployment architecture for non-clinical BCI analogue or assistive interface.

Oral defense: Who restores safe function after software/hardware update failure?

Learning outcome: Integrate signal → estimator → controller/feedback → human adaptation → safety → utility.

Build / reproduction: Capstone: public/synthetic-data BCI, adaptive assistive controller or sensory augmentation simulator with failure tests.

Oral defense: Where does the human compensate for your technology?

Learning outcome: Produce roadmap that distinguishes lab capability, assistive utility and speculative augmentation.
